target_customer: School districts and pediatric groups that contract Daybreak, with insurers and government programs paying so that families pay little or nothing
problem: Kids and teens cannot get timely mental health care because of provider shortages and cost. Daybreak delivers teletherapy and psychiatry through schools and bills insurance or government funding.
business_model: B2B2C care delivery: school and health plan partnerships, with reimbursement from insurance and Medicaid

founders.name: Alex Alvarado
founders.background_notes: YC page says he spent the last decade on digital health products. Crunchbase News called him 31 at the time of its interview, no founding age stated.

founders.name: Siddarth Cidambi
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder on the YC page (as Sid Cidambi) and by Crunchbase News.

founders.name: Luke Mercado
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in Crunchbase News, not on the YC page. Alvarado said equity was split three ways.

competitors.name: PresenceLearning
competitors.what: Online teletherapy for schools, mainly special education speech and related services
competitors.traction_then: Serving schools remotely during the 2020 shift to remote learning

technical_complexity.rationale: Mostly telehealth scheduling, clinical operations and insurance billing built on existing video tools. The hard parts are operational: clinician supply, payer contracts and school integration.

defensibility.rationale: School district partnerships (more than 60 districts by 2023) and payer contracts take time to build, but the clinical service itself can be copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: School based teletherapy kept attracting rivals (Hazel Health added mental health in 2021, DotCom Therapy raised a Series A in 2021). No incumbent absorbed Daybreak through 2023 reports.

market_need_then: Youth mental health demand rose sharply in 2020 and schools lacked counselors. Daybreak began serving California schools in 2019 and the founders targeted zero cost to families through insurance and government funding.

branding.domain_note: Uses daybreakhealth.com, with a health suffix, not daybreak.com.

identity.visual_style: family and school oriented health brand
identity.voice_and_tone: warm and clinical, with claims of clinical validation

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself was found. The name is evocative of a fresh start but is shared with unrelated organizations such as Daybreak Partners and Daybreak Fund.

outcome_analysis: Daybreak sold youth teletherapy through school partnerships and funded care via insurance and Medicaid, which gave it a distribution channel and a payer path that consumer mental health apps lacked. It raised a seed in early 2021, a 10M Series A in March 2022 and a 13M Series B led by Union Square Ventures in August 2023, reaching about 25M raised. No shutdown or acquisition is reported, and the Series A lead and seed amount differ across outlets.
notes: Seed amount conflicts: 1.8M USD (Pitchbook and most sources, dated 2021-02-09) versus 2M USD on StartupIntros. A 125K USD YC era entry from aggregators is unverified. Series A lead: Crunchbase News says Lightspeed led, Axios search summary did not name a lead. Series B coverage says total raised about 25M. Education and employers for the co-founders other than Alvarado were not found. Outcome search found no layoffs, sale or shutdown.
